On December 21st, 2022, the temperature in Cheyenne, Wyoming, plummeted by 42 degrees Fahrenheit in just one hour. With another 9-degree plunge in the next hour, this has been confirmed as a record-breaking temperature drop. Some people were [[1]], travel plans were disrupted, and, for some at least, Christmas was ruined. A visit from the arctic blast was responsible for this flash freeze. Unfortunately, this is expected to happen with higher [[2]] in the future. As a result of global warming, the winter is becoming shorter. The intensity of it not only gives chills but makes it deadly.
An arctic blast occurs when the polar vortex enlarges. The vortex is the low pressure cold air areas surrounding the poles. During the winter in the northern hemisphere, the polar vortex can expand, sending frigid air south to parts of North America, Europe, and Asia. Freezing rain, sleet, and snow can [[3]] the low temperature. Frost bite can form in less than five minutes. High ways can be deadly slippery. Taken together, this can pose [[4]] danger to people and infrastructure. Any time winter storms are forecast, it’s important to be prepared: wear warm clothing, have a backup plan [[5]] power outage, fill the gas tank, keep a jump start cable and an ice scraper in the car, and ensure pets and livestock will not be overly exposed to cold air.
